study.title: Networks Are Associated With Acupuncture Treatment in Patients With Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Resting-State Imaging Study
study.study_design: Prospective observational study with pre-post comparison in IBS-D patients and cross-sectional comparison with healthy controls; resting-state fMRI
study.randomization: Not reported for neuroimaging arm; paper mentions 11 IBS-D received sham acupuncture but sham group fMRI data not analyzed in primary results
study.population: Patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) and healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients with IBS-D: (1) Rome IV diagnostic criteria; (2) aged between 18 and 70 years old; (3) right handiness; (4) the baseline of IBS-SSS ≥ 75; (5) no drug intervention at least 2 weeks and no acupuncture intervention for 3 months before enrollment; (6) no participation in other studies during the same period; (7) no obvious abnormality of colonoscopy and biochemical examination; and (8) no claustrophobia. HCs: (1) right handiness; (2) no neurology psychiatric disorder history; (3) gender and age-matched with IBS-D patients; (4) no other organic or functional disorder.
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients with IBS-D: (1) intestinal organic lesions, or systemic diseases affecting gastrointestinal motility; (2) an abdominal or rectum and anus operation history; (3) no other organic disorder; (4) in pregnancy, lactation, postpartum ≤ 12 months and susceptible to allergies; (5) other treatments at the same time; (6) a neurology psychiatric disorder history; (7) metal allergy or severe needle fear.
study.source_location: Pages 1-3, Abstract, Introduction, Materials and Methods (Participants, Outcome Measures sections)

arms.dropouts: 10 excluded before acupuncture (8 head movement, 2 parameter differences); 11 dropped out during treatment; 11 received sham acupuncture (excluded from primary analysis). fMRI post-treatment analyzed: 42 (completed true acupuncture).

extraction_notes.note: No formal trial registration number is reported anywhere in the paper.
Expectancy, treatment credibility, blinding success, and participant allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.
No formal adverse event reporting or safety monitoring section is present. The conclusion mentions 'without side effects' but no systematic safety data are presented.

The n_analyzed for the IBS-D post-treatment neuroimaging vs HCs comparison is unclear. The text states 64 IBS-D were compared to 29 HCs pre-treatment, and 42 IBS-D completed true acupuncture for post-treatment analysis. It is unclear whether the post-treatment vs HC comparison used 42 IBS-D or a different n.

The sham acupuncture arm (n=11) is mentioned but its procedure is not described (no needle type, penetration, location, or sensation details). These patients were excluded from the neuroimaging analysis. No clinical outcomes for the sham group are reported.

Specific t-statistics, F-statistics, or exact p-values for neural inter-network contrasts are not reported in the text; only 'P < 0.05, FDR corrected' is stated. Exact values are visible only in Figure 4 and Figure 5 matrices but cannot be read precisely from figures in the PDF.

Figures 4 and 5 contain connectivity matrix heatmaps with color-coded p-values (sign(t)*log10(p)) but exact numeric statistics for each network pair are not tabulated in the text. Precise values for non-significant pairs cannot be extracted.
Coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) is not explicitly stated for the ICA spatial maps. No coordinate tables are provided for peak activations within individual ICA components.
Table 2 reports n_analyzed as implied 42 (completed true acupuncture) but this is not explicitly stated in the table caption; it is inferred from the Results section text.

The paper reports sex as '37/27' for IBS-D (n=74) in Table 1, which is interpreted as 37 male/27 female or 37 female/27 male — direction not specified in table. Total is 64, not 74, suggesting possible OCR or reporting discrepancy.
No normalization template or coordinate space is explicitly reported for the fMRI preprocessing and ICA analysis.
extraction_notes.source_location: Pages 3-4, Materials and Methods (fMRI Data Preprocessing, Independent Component Analysis)

extraction_notes.note: Deqi was described as a goal of needle manipulation but was not formally quantified using any validated instrument (e.g., MASS, Deqi Rating Scale). No numeric deqi scores are reported.
The paper states 'the total IBS-SSS decreased by 123.51' in a reference to a prior study (Pei et al., 2020), not the current study. This should not be interpreted as the current study's effect size.

The needle size field '30 mm × 40 mm' likely refers to needle gauge and length (e.g., 0.30 mm diameter × 40 mm length), not a surface area. This is a common notation in Chinese acupuncture literature.
